title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 — Section 31 (Form and contents of arbitral award)

content.overview: An arbitral award shall be made in writing and signed by the members of the tribunal. In multi-arbitrator proceedings, the signatures of the majority of all members is sufficient if the reason for any omitted signature is stated. The award shall state the reasons on which it is based, unless the parties have agreed that no reasons are to be given or the award is an agreed-terms award under section 30. The award shall state its date and the place of arbitration. A signed copy shall be delivered to each party. The tribunal may include interest and costs as provided by the section.
content.glance: Written signed award; reasons unless agreed or s. 30 award; date and place; delivery to parties; interest and costs as provided.
content.study: Writing and signature are mandatory. Majority signatures suffice if the reason for omission is stated. Reasons are required unless parties agreed otherwise or the award is under section 30. Date, place of arbitration, delivery of signed copies, and interest/costs powers apply as provided.
